page_title: Ride-Sharing Apps, Uber and Lyft - Digital Confidence Centre
title: Ride-Sharing Apps, Uber and Lyft
description: How to request a safe ride with Uber or Lyft, verify your driver before you get in, and share your trip with family. Free, plain-language lesson for Canadian seniors. No account needed.
lesson_time: About 20 minutes, at your own pace
lead: How to request a safe ride using Uber or Lyft, verify your driver before you get in, share your trip with a family member, and know what to do if you ever feel unsafe.

story.label: Robert's story
paragraphs: Robert, 76, had always driven himself everywhere. When his car went in for a week-long repair, he faced a dilemma: a doctor's appointment across town, and no way to get there. Taxis seemed expensive and unreliable. His daughter suggested Uber.

"I do not want a stranger driving me around," Robert said. But his daughter showed him how the app worked: you could see the driver's name, photo, car model, and licence plate before they even arrived. Other passengers had rated this driver 4.9 out of 5 over 2,000 trips. That made Robert feel much better.

The driver arrived exactly on time. Robert checked the licence plate against the app, a match. The driver greeted him by name without being asked. The ride was comfortable and professional. Robert tracked the route on his phone the whole way, knowing his daughter could see his location too.

He made his appointment with ten minutes to spare. He now uses Uber monthly, especially for early morning flights when he does not want to impose on his children. "It is actually more comfortable than a taxi," he says. "And I feel safer because I can see everything before I get in."

coach: Getting into a car you booked on a phone takes real trust, and feeling unsure the first time is completely reasonable. Thousands of Canadian seniors use these services safely every day, and every safety feature in this lesson (the driver photo, the licence plate, the shared trip) exists because riders asked for it.

sections.label: What is ride-sharing?
sections.text: Ride-sharing apps connect you with local, screened drivers through your smartphone. You request a ride, a nearby driver accepts, and picks you up. Payment is automatic, no cash needed. You see the driver's name, photo, car details, and licence plate before they arrive, and you know the price upfront.

sections.title: Step 1: Download and set up
steps: On iPhone or iPad: open the App Store (blue icon with a white "A"). Tap Search, type "Uber", and tap GET. The Uber icon is black with white text.
On Android: open the Google Play Store (colourful triangle). Search "Uber" and tap Install.
Tap Create Account. Enter your phone number, you will receive a verification code by text message. Enter the code to verify your identity.
Enter your name and email address. Then add your payment method, a credit or debit card. This is stored securely and encrypted.
Allow location access when prompted. This lets Uber show you nearby drivers and know where to pick you up. You can always type a manual pickup address instead.

sections.title: Step 2: Requesting your ride
steps: Open the Uber app. Tap the search bar at the top that says "Where to?" Type your destination, the address, or a well-known place like "Windsor Regional Hospital" or "Devonshire Mall."
Choose your ride type. You will see options like UberX (standard car, most affordable), Uber Comfort (newer, more spacious car), and sometimes Uber XL (larger vehicle). UberX is fine for most trips.
Review the price. Uber shows you the upfront cost before you confirm. No surprises, this is the amount that will be charged to your card.
Confirm your pickup location is correct, then tap "Request UberX" (or whichever type you chose).
Wait 10 to 60 seconds for a driver to accept. You will then see the driver's name, photo, star rating, car model, colour, and licence plate number.

sections.label: What you see after a driver accepts
sections.text: The app shows you: the driver's first name and photo, their star rating (for example 4.87 stars from 1,847 trips), the car model and colour (for example "Silver Toyota Camry"), and the licence plate number. Always check the plate before getting in.
Step 3: Meeting your driver, the most important part

sections.label: Safety first, always
sections.text: Before getting into any vehicle, do these three things in order: check the licence plate FIRST, check the car make and colour, and let the driver greet you by YOUR name.

sections.title: The three checks before you get in
steps: Check the licence plate FIRST. Look at the plate on the car approaching you and compare it to the plate shown in the app. They must match exactly.
Check the car make and colour. The app tells you "Silver Toyota Camry", make sure the car in front of you matches.

Let the driver greet you by YOUR name. A legitimate Uber driver knows who they are picking up. Wait for them to say "Are you Robert?", you should NEVER be the first to say the driver's name. This prevents strangers from impersonating your driver.

sections.label: The Golden Rule of Ride-Sharing Safety
sections.text: If something does not match, if the plate is different, if the driver seems unsure of your name, or if anything feels wrong, do NOT get in the car. Cancel the trip in the app and request a new one. Your safety is worth a brief delay.

items: Sit in the back seat, this is the standard practice and most comfortable.
Wear your seatbelt, always.
Share your trip: in the app, tap the shield icon, then "Share Status", then select a contact. Your chosen family member or friend can now watch your ride in real time on their phone.
Emergency button: if you ever feel unsafe, the app has a 911 button that sends your location and driver details to emergency services.
Trust your instincts: if you feel uncomfortable at any point, you can ask to be let out at the next safe public place (like a gas station or pharmacy).

sections.title: Step 5: Arrival and payment
steps: When you arrive, payment processes automatically through the app. You do not need cash or a card, nothing changes hands at all.
You will be asked to rate your driver from 1 to 5 stars. A tip is optional, suggested 15 to 20% for great service. You can also skip the tip.
A receipt is automatically emailed to you. You can also view all past trips in the app under "Your Trips."

sections.text: Lyft works almost identically to Uber. The setup, requesting, and safety procedures are the same. A few differences to note:

items: Logo: pink with a stylised "L", sometimes called the "pink mustache brand."
Pricing: sometimes slightly cheaper than Uber, sometimes slightly more, it is worth checking both apps if you have time.
Availability: in Ontario, Lyft is active in Windsor, London, and Kitchener-Waterloo. Uber tends to have wider coverage in smaller cities like St. Thomas and Woodstock.
Safety features: the same, GPS tracking, driver photo and plate verification, 911 emergency button, and trip sharing.

sections.label: Which App Should I Use?
sections.text: Both are safe and reliable. If you are in a larger city, try both and see which has shorter wait times and better prices that day. If you are in a smaller community, start with Uber as it tends to have more drivers in rural Ontario areas.

steps.name: Verify
steps.text: Did I expect this message? Does the sender look right? When in doubt, close it and call someone you trust.

sections.text: Ride-sharing is designed with safety as a priority. Here is a complete summary of your safety checklist:

items: Always check the licence plate FIRST, before the car door, before anything else.
Let the driver greet you by name, never say their name first.
Never get in a car that does not match the app, cancel and request again.
Share your trip with a family member before every ride.
Trust your instincts, if something feels wrong, end the ride.

sections.label: Confidence check
sections.text: These safety habits take about 30 seconds total and make every ride safer. With time, they become completely automatic.
Uber and Lyft availability in your area

items: Windsor: Uber active, Lyft active.

Kitchener-Waterloo: Uber active, Lyft active.
St. Thomas: Uber active, Lyft limited.

sections.text: Cyber-Seniors offers free tech help by phone at 1-844-217-3057. Trained senior volunteers help other seniors, in plain language, at your pace.
Try it today: set up without requesting
Set up the Uber app and get comfortable with how it works, without actually requesting a ride yet.

sections.title: Your practice this week
steps: Download Uber from the App Store or Google Play Store.
Create your account (phone number, email, name).
Add a payment method, a credit or debit card.
Open the app and type in a local destination: your doctor's office, a friend's address, or the nearest mall.
Look at the ride options and the price shown. Notice how clearly the cost is displayed.
Do NOT tap "Request" yet, just explore the app and see how it feels.
Optional: ask a family member to try a short test trip with you as a "passenger practice run."

sections.label: Success looks like this
sections.text: You have the app installed, an account set up, and you understand how to request a ride and what information you would see about your driver.

sections.heading: Quick check: test your knowledge
sections.intro: Tap the answer you think is correct. There is no score kept and nothing to sign in to.

questions.q: 1. You are waiting for your Uber. A car pulls up and the driver says "Are you going to the hospital?" What should you do FIRST?
options: Get in right away, they know where you are going
Check the licence plate on the car against the plate shown in your app before doing anything else
Tell the driver your name so they know it is you
questions.right: Exactly right. Always check the licence plate FIRST. That is the single most important safety step in ride-sharing.
questions.wrong: The very first thing to do is check the licence plate. Compare it to the plate shown in your app. Only get in if they match exactly.

questions.q: 2. How does Uber payment work at the end of a ride?
options: You pay cash to the driver
You hand your credit card to the driver to swipe
Payment is automatic through the app, nothing changes hands at all
questions.right: Perfect. Payment is fully automatic through the app. No cash, no card exchange. You receive an email receipt automatically.
questions.wrong: Uber payment is completely automatic, it charges the card saved in your app. You do not exchange cash or a card with the driver. An email receipt arrives automatically.

questions.q: 3. What does the "Share Trip" feature in Uber do?
options: Lets a chosen family member or friend see your real-time ride location on their phone
Posts your trip to social media automatically
questions.right: Correct. Share Trip lets a trusted person watch your ride in real time. Your daughter, son, or friend can see exactly where you are at every moment.
questions.wrong: Share Trip lets you send your real-time ride progress to a family member or friend. They can watch where you are on a map throughout the entire trip.

items: I understand what ride-sharing apps are and how they work
